Business justification: Day 0 GPU support in notebooks is table stakes for the OpenShift for NVIDIA partnership stack. Notebook images are the primary entry point for data scientists on OpenShift AI — without Vera Rubin readiness at launch, the entire developer experience layer of the stack is incomplete. This is a strategic investment aligned with NVIDIA Vera Rubin milestones (Tech Preview Jun 2026, GA Oct 2026) and directly supports the OpenShift for NVIDIA fast lane program.
User problem: Today, the v2025.1 'Jupyter | PyTorch | CUDA | Python 3.12' notebook image works with CUDA 13.0 and GPUs are detected, but Vera Rubin GPUs are not formally validated, ARM (aarch64) notebook images for the Vera CPU are not shipped, and driver/toolkit alignment with NVIDIA's Vera Rubin software stack is not guaranteed. Data scientists deploying on Vera Rubin NVL72 hardware cannot be confident notebooks will work correctly without manual environment setup, and there is no multi-arch support for the ARM-based Vera CPU.
Scope: Single focused need — validating and certifying existing notebook images for Vera Rubin architecture. MVP includes: CUDA 13.x validation on Vera Rubin, PyTorch with Vera Rubin GPU kernel support, ARM aarch64 multi-arch notebook images, NVIDIA driver alignment, GPU detection and multi-GPU support validation, and base OS alignment with RHEL for NVIDIA baseline. Non-MVP stretch items include TensorRT/cuDNN updates and additional notebook image variants like TensorFlow. Out of scope: CUDA 14.x, non-notebook components (inference server, llm-d), x86 Rubin NVL8, custom user-built images, non-OpenShift for NVIDIA platforms.
Success criteria: The 'Jupyter | PyTorch | CUDA | Python 3.12' notebook image launches successfully on OpenShift for NVIDIA with Vera Rubin NVL72 hardware. torch.cuda.is_available() returns True and torch.cuda.get_device_name() correctly identifies the Vera Rubin GPU. PyTorch training and inference workloads execute successfully on Vera Rubin GPUs from within notebooks. ARM aarch64 notebook image variant is available and functional on Vera CPU. NVIDIA driver version meets minimum requirements per Vera Rubin release notes. Notebook image is available in the OpenShift AI image catalog at Vera Rubin launch dates (Tech Preview Jun 2026, GA Oct 2026).
